s: The consumer of the system - mobile app, browser, CLI, or third-party integration making requests to the API surface.
w: Clients initiate HTTP/WebSocket/gRPC connections to the system edge. Browsers resolve DNS, connect through CDN, and load SPA bundles; mobile apps talk API directly or through gateways. Clients handle retries, token refresh, local caching, and offline queues. Retry-after headers and exponential backoff prevent thundering herd on recovery.
use: Third-party partner integrations calling public API endpoints
CLI tools and automation scripts accessing system programmatically
IoT devices pushing telemetry and receiving commands
avoid: Treating client as reliable - always design for client bugs, timeouts, and duplicate requests
Trusting client-supplied values without server-side validation

props.retry_strategy: How the client backs off after failures
props.auth_token: JWT or API key used for authentication

pat.d: Client doubles delay between retries with jitter to avoid synchronized storms.

pits: Missing client-side retry budget causing infinite loops - cap retries and use circuit-breaking
Hardcoded timeouts too short for flaky mobile networks - adaptive timeouts per connection type
tips: Discuss idempotency keys: clients should resend with the same key to prevent duplicate charges
Token refresh race conditions in mobile apps are a common source of auth bugs
